decision: When the person says go for a step he must witness, the lane coordinator writes one line into the item's note before running the launcher: Witnessed go: "<words>" at HH:MM, until HH:MM; told: <what to expect and check>. The keeper takes only that step, only while the window is open, and reports what was seen at once. No line or a past window: it does the rest of the item and leaves the step. A go never carries to another item, and only the coordinator that heard it writes it.
why: On surya (2026-11-18) a launched keeper declined a bite the author had said Go to: a launched run hears no message, so practice 11 (say what to expect, wait for go) could not be met. The item is what a launched keeper reads; a go recorded there with words, time and expiry keeps both halves of practice 11 - he was told, he said go - and keeps the launchers.
rejected: Witnessed steps only for a directly briefed keeper: brings back the manual start the launchers retired, and a second way to start a keeper. A schema field on the item: a note line suffices and is read the same way; a field adds a record change for one line. A go that lasts until revoked or carries across items: the person witnesses one step at one moment; an open-ended go is no longer witnessed.

brief: scripts/workarounds reads sites only, knows backlog items as well as upstream items, and gives each workaround its way out
decision: scripts/workarounds skips lines under data/, docs/ and research/ of each path and the placeholder item-id; looks an item up in upstream_items, then in backlog; prints per site "ITEM - state; way out: patch upstream | patch carried in FORK | our work (backlog ITEM)" or "due: retire" (upstream has it, the backlog item is done, or the item is in neither table - then also "file its item"). Ends 1 when one is due.
why: linux-phone-oco decision 2026-11-18-workarounds-read-as-one (docs #542): a rule and a script read the same way. Its failing test research/workarounds/2026-11-18/workarounds-read.sh failed 7 checks on origin/main: records and the AGENTS.md example listed as sites, a backlog item read as not known, no way out named. Checks B-D now pass; A waits on the lanes marking their rules.
rejected: A separate reader for lane rules: one marker, one reader. Excluding data/ and docs/ by grep --exclude-dir: it also skips a PATH named docs (the docs clone itself). Treating an unknown item as merely not known: a marker with no item has no way out, so it is due.

brief: A witnessed go is idealkb data: an item --witness person, opened by ikb backlog-go with a window; tad q ready offers it only while open
decision: keep-a-shared-resource ("A witnessed step") and the keeper and lane-coordinator cards point at idealkb 0.21.0: the item is marked --witness person; the lane coordinator that heard the go opens it with ikb backlog-go --until, and writes what the person was told in the note; tad q ready offers the item only while the go is open. The how stays in the base's AGENTS.md; ideal-agent says where, not what.
why: idealkb v0.21.0 (#93) made the go data, asked through the Top Coordinator: the window is read by the one picking query instead of a keeper parsing a note line, so the keeper needs no rule of its own to refuse an expired go.
rejected: Keeping the "Witnessed go:" note line beside the field: two ways to say one go. Restating backlog-go's options in the skill: they would go stale when idealkb changes them; the base's AGENTS.md row is the pointer.

brief: An author's held no on a risky device action becomes a check the artefact must pass, in build, CI and the keeper's recipe - not only a record
decision: change-a-device gains "A held no is a gate": a hold from the author on a risky action is turned into a check on the artefact (its device tree, config, command line) run in its build and CI and by the keeper before it boots or flashes; the check is removed when the hold is lifted. The class question gains a trigger: an action the author held back happened anyway.
why: walleye, lab PR 330: the author said wait on probing the Pixel 2 storage; it was recorded as a decision in prose, an enable for one parked image landed in the shared dts, and four or more unattended boots probed the card. No check tested the artefact against the hold, and keepers boot by try items, not by what the image enables. Walleye's words: "a decision held in prose, not in a check".
rejected: A new skill or practice: one bullet in the skill the keeper already loads suffices. Putting it in keep-a-shared-resource: it is about changing a device, which change-a-device carries for every keeper. A generic guard in ideal-agent's program: what to check is device-specific (a dts node, a cmdline); the lane writes the check, the skill says that it must exist.

brief: Our own Python stays refused; a required third-party Python tool (dtschema) is installed in its own ~/.local environment and run by name
decision: Practice 21 and the guard: writing Python, or making our tools depend on it, stays refused. Installing a third-party tool a step requires is let through when it is by name and isolated: pipx install|upgrade|uninstall|reinstall|inject|list|ensurepath with package names; python -m venv into ~/.local; such a venv's bin/pip install|uninstall|list|show with package names. Refused still: python and pip otherwise, pipx run, paths, -r, -e. The tool then runs by its own name (make dt_binding_check, dt-doc-validate), which the guard never saw as Python.
why: The author, 2026-11-19, relayed by the Top Coordinator: "its ok to run python if its required, i just dont want our work to depend on it". The kernel's dt_binding_check and dtbs_check need dtschema, a Python tool, before any device-tree patch is mailed.
rejected: Lifting the guard on python and pip: lets our own scripts back in. A one-off override variable (PYTHON_OK=1): any script could carry it, so the rule would hold only by memory. pip install --user into the system Python: not isolated, and Arch refuses it (PEP 668). A system package via pacman: needs root, and dtschema must follow the kernel's version.

brief: ideal-agent is MIT OR Apache-2.0 throughout - program, scripts, skills, role cards, practices, base - per path in REUSE.toml, held by a shell check in CI
decision: LICENSE becomes LICENSE-MIT beside LICENSE-APACHE; Cargo.toml and plugin.json say MIT OR Apache-2.0; REUSE.toml annotates every path; README names the licences; scripts/licence-check (shell) fails CI when a tracked file has neither a REUSE.toml path nor an SPDX-License-Identifier line, or a named licence has no text. The prose too is MIT OR Apache-2.0, the call linux-phone-oco docs decision 2026-11-19-licences-for-our-repositories left to the owner.
why: The author's word "Yes, as suggested", relayed by orchestration, on docs decision 2026-11-19-licences-for-our-repositories: code MIT OR Apache-2.0, with the owner choosing for prose. Here the prose is the plugin's behaviour: the program reads data/practices.json and ships it in the crate, and the skills and cards load as the plugin runs - one licence keeps the package whole.
rejected: CC-BY-SA-4.0 for skills, cards and the base: share-alike in a package beside permissive code splits one plugin into two terms, and the crate ships practices.json. REUSE lint: a Python tool, which our work must not depend on (practice 21). One annotation for all paths (**): a new top-level folder would pass unseen; three named groups make it ask.

brief: Rust stays the language for our logic and scripts; shell is only one-off glue; Mojo not now (re-check 2027); no second scripting language
decision: Practice 21 is tightened: shell only for one-off glue (a few commands in order, no parsing, no loops over data, no functions); anything with logic is Rust - rust-script for one file, a Rust tool for what repeats. No second language is adopted. Existing shell past glue moves to Rust as each owner touches it (backlog shell-past-glue-into-rust here; each lane its own), not in one rewrite. The canon does not change: it holds principles, and a language choice is our practice.
why: The author's remark (2026-11-19) and research languages-for-scripts: Rust scores highest on reliability and on static aarch64-musl phone binaries, warm script start 4 ms; its IDE is one step below Roslyn, closing as cargo scripts stabilise.
rejected: Mojo: 1.1 and 1.2 broke code, no static binaries, cross-compile stops at objects, part of it non-OSI - against "never depends on what is not open and stable". C#/F# beside Rust: the best IDE (Visual Studio is the benchmark), but a second toolchain, a 7 s cold start, and a musl-arm64 cross that needs a sysroot; worth it only if IDE outweighs one toolchain, and with Rust at IDE 4 it does not. Go: easiest cross, but errors are easy to drop and no inline deps; a second language for little gain. Deno, Kotlin: no musl phone target. Rewriting all shell now: ~10,500 lines; moving it as touched follows practice 20.

brief: Existing shell is left as it is unless a real need comes; practice 21 binds new work - a new script with logic starts in Rust
decision: The move of existing shell into Rust is dropped: backlog shell-past-glue-into-rust closes, and no lane is asked to open one. Practice 21 binds new work: a new script with logic starts in Rust. Existing shell is changed in shell, and rewritten only when a real need comes (it breaks, or grows past glue in the change at hand).
why: The author, 2026-11-19, relayed by the Top Coordinator: "i dont think its necessary, too much work.. if we dont rely on it much i say we leave them as is for now".
rejected: Moving shell as each owner touches it: still work he judged not needed for scripts we do not rely on much. Leaving practice 21 unworded on existing shell: a session reading "anything with logic is Rust" could rewrite a working script.

brief: A person is asked to attend only when the step is one prepared, tested command away; the go is for that run; a failure holds the run, never a live fix
decision: Practice 11 is tightened. Each role carries its own part: the coordinator calls the author only on a lane's "ready, one command away"; the lane coordinator has the program built and tested without him, opens the go on the item naming the program, and launches the keeper before he is called; the builder writes a program whose entry reads like the procedure; the keeper runs only the prepared command and holds on failure. keep-a-shared-resource "An attended step" holds the whole; change-a-device, bring-up-a-part and write-code-by-the-canon point to it. ideal-agent's own main.rs now reads as its procedure (plumbing moved to cli.rs; every output byte-identical).
why: The author's two rules of 2026-11-19 (practice 11 quotes them) and research attended-steps: rehearse before asking, one action to start, an approval bound to one run, holds instead of improvising.
rejected: A run id in every go, as GitHub and Jenkins bind theirs: the go on an item that names its program already binds it to that program; whether a per-run id is needed is for the shared runner (docs lpoco-attended) to show. Keeping practice 11 as a heads-up only: it let a person wait while a procedure was written. Writing the attended runner here: it is device work, the lanes' and lpoco's (surya-lab #388/#390, google-walleye-lab #411, docs #634); ideal-agent holds the general rule.

brief: Test and bring-up procedures are chains of small steps with device values as data; a step proven on one device is lifted into the shared tool when a second needs it
decision: bring-up-a-part gains "Small steps that compose": one job per step, a chain not a script, device values in the device data over family defaults, the board's own path one marked unit, a step lifted into the shared tool on the second device that needs it as is (third copy if the copies differ), a shared step growing a device's flags copied back out. keep-a-shared-resource "An attended step", write-code-by-the-canon and the builder card point to it. Where the shared steps live is the project's: linux-phone-oco names lpoco's step library (docs lpoco-attended, bringup-step-runner).
why: The author, 2026-11-19, relayed by the Top Coordinator: "is test procedures are small so that they can be later on chained together and extracted into general tools that will work for any device ? do we have that reflected somewhere in our structures ?" - it was only in pieces (practice 20, bring-up-a-part, 2026-11-19-attended-one-command-away). Research steps-that-compose.
rejected: A new practice: practice 20 already counts hand-work into tools; the how belongs in the bring-up method that every builder and keeper of a device loads. Sharing every step from the start: Metz - the wrong abstraction costs more than a copy, and one device does not show which values vary. Writing the step library here: device work, lpoco's (orchestration's lpoco-attended).

brief: Large outputs go on disk under AGENT_BUILD (~/.cache/agent-build/RUN), with TMPDIR there; /tmp is a RAM tmpfs for small scratch files only
decision: agent-env exports AGENT_BUILD=~/.cache/agent-build/RUN and TMPDIR=AGENT_BUILD/tmp, so kernel builds, images, package trees, cargo install builds and mktemp land on disk. A cargo target stays in its worktree (on disk, made by branch); CARGO_TARGET_DIR is left alone.
why: The lab machine's /tmp is a 16 GB RAM tmpfs that session scratchpads share; it reached 98% on 2026-11-19 from old builders' cargo targets and kernel and image copies. The author freed disk (500+ GB). The Top Coordinator asked that it hold without anyone remembering it.
rejected: A global CARGO_TARGET_DIR: packaging scripts in tad-engine, lab-agent, snapall and lab-tools read ./target/release and would break. A line in briefs only: it holds only while remembered.

brief: A role acts on origin/main: the start writes its brief from main to a session file and prints a pointer; the guard refuses reads in a shared clone behind origin/main
decision: 1. The role start writes the brief, read from its repository's origin/main, whole to the session's file under ~/.local/state/ideal-agent/sessions, headed by its path and main's commit, and prints a pointer and its first paragraph, so the start stays under the app's 10,000-character hook-output cap. 2. The guard refuses, in a shared clone's main checkout whose HEAD is behind its local origin/main (no fetch), any command but git, branch and those that only look, a path there named in a command, and Read, Grep and Glob of its paths - naming a worktree of one's own, git show origin/main:PATH and git pull --ff-only; SHARED_CLONE_OK=1 lets a deliberate one through.
